changes.summary: explore workflows with a local canvas and nested navigation
changes.body:
Render workflow cards, edges and instructions locally with React Flow and ELK.
Show nested states as scope boxes with collapse, expand and focus controls.
Navigate retained child workflows from invoking cards and return through shared
workflow/scope breadcrumbs; unmatched retained children remain available as
contextual links. Blue Current and green Direct target indicators remain
independent of orange Bee dispatch and recorded request status.

The shared preview dialog survives card regrouping, opens within the native
bead inspector when triggered there, and keeps its instruction divider usable.
The Storybook catalogue separates Canvas, Cards, Edges, Simulation, Nested
actors, Refresh and Inspection, with shell and inspector integration examples.

Required: upgrade Busy Bee alongside Hive UI so its PATH installation supports
`system preview`, `system checkpoint` and `system simulate`.
Optional: run `mise run hive-ui:storybook` to explore the component catalogue.

adoption.text:
upgrade Busy Bee alongside Hive UI so its PATH installation supports
`system preview`, `system checkpoint` and `system simulate`.

changes.summary: simulate outcomes and poll saved checkpoints efficiently
changes.body:
Use Saved and Simulate modes to inspect published instructions or explore
temporary outcomes with editable event data, examples, Back and Reset controls.
Root workflows also accept explicit initial input. Simulation pins its starting
inspection and selected actor while saved updates arrive; returning to Saved
discards the walkthrough and displays the latest inspection.

The open dialog owns its initial full read and visibility-aware five-second
checkpoint polling. Unchanged checkpoints retain the diagram without importing
the definition again; changed checkpoints, manual Refresh and failure recovery
request full inspection. Refresh preserves selection, viewport, zoom and panel
size. Manual Refresh also detects definition-only changes. Preview and
simulation leave the actual run unchanged.

Running `hive-ui` with a configured database or endpoint source starts the
foreground server again instead of exiting with help. Existing server
options work as before; `--help`, `--version` and `changelog` still exit
without starting the server.

Show valid exported hierarchy with a warning when the Beads export lags or changes
during a read. Native cards and details remain usable; unreadable or invalid
hierarchy still reports an error.

changes.summary: refresh visible views and open workflow previews
changes.body:
Automatically refresh the current Beads or Bees view, selected bead, outline and
open workflow preview five seconds after each cycle settles. Pause new cycles
while the tab is hidden and refresh on return when idle. Retain previous snapshots
with a notice during loading or failure, and keep open previews mounted when cards
regroup.

changes.summary: read release history without starting the web server
changes.body:
Run `hive-ui changelog` to inspect recorded board changes and exit. The
command needs no repository configuration, tracker or running Colony.

changes.summary: Discovers registered repositories and their Beads databases from an already-running Colony daemon at startup.
